event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CBOE’s filing, submitted roughly four years after the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic, acknowledges that pandemic-related disruptions remain a meaningful, though now largely prospective, threat.  The company frames COVID-19 as part of a broader “pandemic” risk category that could trigger renewed government lockdowns, supply-chain breakdowns, labour-force constraints, remote-work frictions, legal liabilities, and—most critically for an exchange operator—shifts in trading behaviour and volumes.  All statements are forward-looking and unquantified, signalling potential rather than current damage; yet CBOE repeatedly uses strong language such as “material adverse effect,” tying the hazard directly to revenues, cash flows and operations.  Under the Time Decay Principle, an event that began in 2020 is now in the 4-to-10-year window, warranting mid-range severity scores (4-6).  The evidence therefore indicates a moderate but persistent risk that could resurface if new variants or policy responses emerge, affecting both the company’s operational infrastructure and demand for its products.

evidence_list.snippet: A pandemic, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, and its effects may have significant impacts on economies around the world.

components.reason: Explicitly links COVID-19 to broad economic impacts (aggravating).
Generic, macro-level statement with no company-specific detail (mitigating).
Forward-looking (‘may’) and unquantified (mitigating).
Still relevant within 4-year window (time-decay neutral to slight aggravation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence is generic but current enough to merit a baseline moderate score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Impacts of a pandemic could also have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

components.reason: Directly ties pandemic to company performance (‘our business, financial condition...’).
Uses strong phrase ‘material adverse effect’.
Forward-looking and unquantified (slight mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Company-specific, high-impact language raises severity to 5 despite lack of quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: Governments, public institutions, and other organizations around the world may take or reimpose previous, emergency measures to combat a potential pandemic, including vaccination requirements, implementation of travel bans, stay-at-home orders, border closures, and closures of offices, factories, schools, public buildings and businesses.

components.reason: Details concrete government measures that can disrupt operations (aggravating).
Scenario-based and not yet realised (mitigating).
No direct financial metric provided (mitigating).
Still within medium-term window (aggravating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides specific disruptive mechanisms but remains hypothetical, yielding a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures may disrupt the supply chain and may interfere with the ability of our employees, vendors, technology equipment suppliers, data and disaster recovery centers, and other service providers to perform their respective responsibilities and obligations relative to the conduct of our business.

components.reason: Identifies supply-chain disruptions and labour/vendor interference—key pandemic impact channels.
Company-specific operational effect (‘our business’).
Forward-looking ‘may’ indicates potential not current impact (mitigating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong operational linkage to supply-chain and workforce risks warrants a mid-high score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition to uncertain expenses and impacts to our business we may incur due to a pandemic as part of us providing a safe and healthy work and trading environment, employees working remotely from different locations and in connection with our return to our offices, we may also be subject to claims from employees or customers alleging failure to maintain safe premises and restrictions with respect to protocols relating to such pandemic.

components.reason: Highlights cost pressures and legal liabilities tied to remote work and workplace safety.
Specifies operational adjustments (remote work) and potential lawsuits (aggravating).
Unquantified and conditional language (‘may’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures multiple cost/liability vectors but remains prospective; moderate score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, changes in trading behavior, impacts to trading behavior due to market disruptions, temporary suspensions of open outcry trading, temporary regulatory measures and other future developments caused by the effects of a pandemic, including a re-occurrence of cases and the emergence of variants, could impact trading volumes and the demand for our products, market data and services, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows and could heighten many of the other risks described herein.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to core revenue driver—trading volumes/demand for products.
Uses strong phrase ‘material adverse effect’.
Identifies multiple channels (regulatory measures, open-outcry suspension) increasing breadth.
Still forward-looking and unquantified (minor mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Most severe excerpt: directly threatens trading volumes with ‘material adverse effect’; earns top mid-range score of 6.
